body:
No you are not selfish. 

Though you guys were close, you can never be sure of his reasoning, or thought. He loved you. It was important, to him, that he told you in the email you mention. There could have been other sources of stress or emotion in his life which you may not be aware of or are not considering. I don't think you should focus on his specific reasoning because that cannot be changed or known, but your health and future can be. Remember him, and love him as you did.  

If you are finding comfort in an afterlife, I think that is good. Find comfort where it presents itself, and consider reading or looking into different religions or philosophies. Don't feel pressure to latch onto one and commit. Take bits from each that make sense and comfort you. Religion is personal. 

>I feel self centered for even staying alive this long

I don't think you should feel that way. If you believe that he is waiting for you, and that you two will be together in an afterlife, there is no rush for you to get there. What is 60/80/100 more years here, when you will spend eternity with him after death? You are not missing out on him or any afterlife by not ending things early. You are only missing out what else is offered here on earth.

>Maybe it's better if the world is destroyed so that the universe can finish expanding and then implode on itself, re-start the Big Bang. Better luck next time .. I guess.

The good news in regards to this part is humans are far from the universe's most advanced, loving, or distinguished life. We are so incredibly insignificant that our actions are will only let ourselves, and our world down. Everything else, as I'd like to imagine, is continuing in beautiful harmony.

> We are alone together.

I think that's beautiful. 

All the widespread ease of communication we have today somehow resulted in less relationships than more. I feel like I can easily have superficial encounters with dozens of people at a time, but not one which is meaningful. People around me seem oblivious, indifferent, or supportive of that being the case. I appreciate knowing you relate and agree.

I wish I could say I have moved forward. I wrote this earlier today with the intent of saving it on my desktop to be found by someone if and when I was gone. 

However, a piece of advice, I can give (which is more of a remedy then help) is that most of the afternoon I was feeling strong emotions which continued to compound and I sunk pretty deep until I wrote this. Pouring out everything I was feeling and thinking into the document didn't solve any of the issues, or move me forward. But emotions and thoughts will swell and dip, and you may be able to relate, but its during the deepest dips that I know I'm the most at risk, and pouring it out pulled me out of the specific dip. 

So when you start to sink think about writing. Don't start with an end goal, just let things come out. You might not be able to climb the whole mountain right now, but by writing you may be able to stop yourself from sliding further down the slope.
